items.title: South Korea launches new bid to guide crowd-pulling shark to sea
items.summary: South Korean authorities began a new attempt Wednesday to coax a shark-turned-viral sensation back to sea, with falling temperatures in the Busan canal where it is stranded raising concerns for its survival.

items.title: Prized wild pepper at risk in Madagascar's shrinking forests
items.summary: A rare wild pepper endemic to Madagascar and prized by international chefs is facing an uncertain future, a victim of its own success and the destruction of its forest habitat.

items.title: A First Nation community in Canada is using a data center to preserve its heritage
items.summary: For thousands of years, Indigenous peoples have passed down their traditions and culture through oral storytelling. Now, a Canadian Indigenous community is using a data center to help preserve its heritage.

items.title: SpaceX turns a profit after a string of losses as its satellite and computer leasing businesses soar
items.summary: SpaceX reported a bigger quarterly profit than expected Tuesday as its satellite communications operations and its business of leasing computing power to other companies boomed.

items.summary: Research in New Phytologist reveals a gene that regulates tea plants' flavor and cold tolerance, providing insights on how to expand the potential for better-tasting tea to be grown in a wider variety of locations.

items.summary: The most comprehensive data set ever collected from Earth's atmosphere during a solar radiation event has highlighted the importance of better-coordinated radiation monitoring for aviation safety, according to new research led by the University of Surrey.

items.title: Shortening Canadian teacher education risks devaluing the profession of teaching
items.summary: Recently, shorter teacher certification programs have been introduced in different Canadian provinces. These programs are being implemented in Alberta, Nova Scotia, Ontario and Québec.

items.title: Researchers study how AI could improve weed management
items.summary: Advances in weed management technology could reduce reliance on herbicides and manual labor, but a new review from the University of Mississippi and Cornell University indicates those tools also bring steep costs and potential challenges.

items.title: Shipwrecks can become thriving reefs, but may contain hidden toxic time bombs
items.summary: Late last year, scientists in Germany published findings on a World War II munitions dump in the Baltic Sea. Some may dismiss the dump as hazardous waste, but to marine biologists it was something far more exciting: a thriving ecosystem.

items.title: Forgotten samples from Greenland's Cold War base reveal warmer summers during ancient ice-free period
items.summary: The site of a former U.S. military base in Greenland was ice-free at a time when summers were a few degrees warmer than today, according to a new University at Buffalo–led study of ancient sediment recovered from beneath the site in the 1960s.

items.title: Judging faces without personality labels uncovers key patterns in first impressions
items.summary: Imagine sitting on a city bus full of strangers. Look around at the people riding with you. If you needed help, how would you choose whom to trust? By scanning people's faces, your brain is already making interpretations about their personalities by judging certain facial features.
